samples.summary: `ensureFontLink` was modified despite an explicit acceptance criterion and out-of-scope constraint forbidding it
samples.evidence: The issue states: "`ensureFontLink` and `findFontLink` keep their existing logic and signatures — the change adds a separate function rather than branching inside them" and under Constraints: "Do not modify `ensureFontLink` or `findFontLink` … so the existing full-load path (picker selection, `onPrefetch`, dialog selection) is provably untouched". The paired todo repeats it (docs/tasks/active/20260825-font-preview-subset-todo.md:60 "Out of scope — Any change to `ensureFontLink` / `findFontLink`"). The diff changes its signature from `void` to `Promise<void>`, adds a `WeakMap<HTMLLinkElement, Promise<void>>` of settle promises, adds load/error listeners, and adds a `removePreviewFontLink(family)` side effect on settle — i.e. the full-load path is now coupled to the preview path in exactly the way the constraint aimed to prevent. It also changes every existing caller's contract (pdf-actions.ts now awaits it, onPrefetch/apply-font-family now discard a floating promise). The reasoning (a `&text=` face with no `unicode-range` pollutes `document.fonts`) may well be right, but it is a spec renegotiation that the PR makes unilaterally rather than the additive change the issue specified.

samples.summary: Opening the picker can now dynamic-import the ~1,900-entry full font library just to look up a recent row's weights — extra data on the very path the issue set out to make cheaper
samples.evidence: `needFullForRecents` triggers `loadFullFontCatalog()` whenever `open` and any recent family is absent from `CATALOG_BY_FAMILY`, not only when the "More fonts…" dialog opens. The issue's outcome is "Opening the font picker … costs far less data per previewed row"; pulling the full-library chunk (previously only paid on dialog open) to save a few hundred bytes of font subset can be a net data regression for users with a non-curated recent. The issue also asked for the subset text and weight to be "derived from what the row actually renders, not from a curated-catalog lookup that may miss" — this adds a second, larger catalog lookup instead. A simpler fit would be omitting the weight (letting css2 serve the family's default cut) or recording the weight alongside the recent when it is picked.

samples.summary: `hasFullFamilyLink` goes well beyond the criterion's "no-op when `findFontLink` resolves", adding href/regex parsing of arbitrary third-party stylesheets
samples.evidence: The acceptance criterion is: "The preview path no-ops when a full link for that family already exists (`findFontLink` resolves)". The implementation instead scans every `link[rel="stylesheet"]` in the head, filters by host, excludes `text=` URLs, regex-extracts every `family=` segment and compares against two spellings of the encoded name. The app-shell case (packages/frontend/index.html loading Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono in full with `eager` absent from the catalog) is a real gap, but the durable fix is arguably marking those three `eager` in the generated catalog data rather than reverse-engineering intent from href strings — a heuristic that has to be kept in sync with anything else that injects a Google Fonts link.

samples.summary: The PDF export's new bounded stylesheet wait is not reflected in slides-pdf-export.md, which still documents the old fire-and-forget `ensureFontLink` step
samples.evidence: pdf-actions.ts now awaits `Promise.race([Promise.all(families.map(ensureFontLink)), 5s timeout])` before `document.fonts.load` — a new, load-bearing ordering constraint with a magic 5s bound. slides-fonts.md and docs-font-controls.md were updated in this diff, but slides-pdf-export.md:132-143 still describes only "injects a Google-Fonts `<link>` for any family not yet linked via `ensureFontLink`, then `await Promise.all(… document.fonts.load …)`", and its risk table (line 213) likewise. That doc is the canonical record of the export's font preparation contract for direct callers of the public API.
searchedFor: read docs/design/slides/slides-fonts.md and docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md diff hunks

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out verbatim. `ensureFontLink` at packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:173 now returns `Promise<void>` (was `void`), adds a `WeakMap<HTMLLinkElement, Promise<void>>` settle registry (line 138), attaches load/error listeners (lines 188-190), and chains `removePreviewFontLink(family)` on settle (lines 191-198) — directly coupling the full-load path to the preview path. finding.summary: Large unrequested scope: a whole design-editor build-lane restructuring rides along with a frontend font-subsetting issue. The issue's area is `frontend`, it declares "Architecture change? No", and none of its acceptance criteria mention the lane graph, `packages/design-editor`, or #966. Yet the diff splits out a new `design-editor:build` lane, rewires `needs` on `design-editor:check`, `design-sandbox:check` and `verify:entropy`, edits `harness.config.json`'s inert-path reason, rewrites `scripts/design.mjs`'s staleness check, adds build-if-stale logic to three `verify-*.mjs` scripts, and updates two design docs (`design-editor-packaging.md`, `harness-engineering.md`) — none of which affects font previews. Only the `verify:fast` addition of `design-editor build` is plausibly needed for the issue's "pnpm verify:fast passes" criterion; the rest is #966 follow-up that belongs in its own PR, where its risk (lane-graph selection) can be reviewed on its own terms.

verdict.reason: The described code is genuinely present: scripts/verify-self.mjs:318-329 introduces a new `design-editor:build` lane and :347, :370, :458-464 rewire `needs` on `design-editor:check`, `design-sandbox:check` and `verify:entropy`; package.json:14 adds the build to `verify:fast`; a new shared packages/design-editor/scripts/build-if-stale.mjs is consumed by three non-CI gates (verify-frame.mjs:26, design-sandbox verify-scenes.mjs:75, verify-tokens.mjs:148) and scripts/design.mjs:124-144 carries rebuild-on-stale logic; two design docs are edited (design-editor-packaging.md:141-152, harness-engineering.md:494-505). The originating issue (docs/tasks/active/20260825-font-preview-subset-todo.md) is scoped to `ensurePreviewFontLink` plus the two row observers, and its only harness criterion is line 56 ("pnpm verify:fast green"); nothing in it mentions the lane graph, packages/design-editor or #966. There is a real counter-argument — the lessons doc (20260825-font-preview-subset-lessons.md:29-44) records that this branch's CI failed `verify:entropy` and that `verify:fast` was red on a clean clone after #966 moved `exports["."]` to `dist/`, which would make the lane split and needs edges prerequisites for this PR to be green, and the doc edits fold into canonical subsystem docs rather than parallel files. But that justification does not cover the whole flagged slice: build-if-stale.mjs:26-29 states outright that those scripts are out of `verify:fast`/`verify:self` and out of the lane graph, and `verify:entropy` is not part of `verify:fast` (package.json:14,21), so the design.mjs / three-gate portion is not explained by the branch being red. A separate open task item also already owns this area (docs/tasks/active/20260812-path-aware-ci-todo.md:266, "5.3 Revisit verify:entropy's needs"). I cannot cleanly refute on any named ground, so the finding stands.

finding.summary: The #966 stale-artefact fix is applied inconsistently: `verify-frame.mjs` still rebuilds only the shell. It boots `fixtures/consumer/vite.config.ts` (line 46 + 122), which imports `@wafflebase/design-editor` BY NAME — the same path the diff argues (in verify-consumer.mjs, verify-scenes.mjs, verify-tokens.mjs) now resolves to `dist/plugin/index.js`. `buildShellIfStale` (lines 82–91) still runs only `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts` and `newestSourceMtime` (line 106) still ignores `tsconfig.build.json`, so this gate keeps exactly the trap the PR says cost an hour: a clean checkout dies with "dev server exited early", a dirty one paints against stale plugin bytes. If the design-editor half is in scope at all, this fourth consumer should have been updated with the others.

verdict.reason: The finding claims verify-frame.mjs was left out of the #966 stale-artefact fix, still containing a local `buildShellIfStale` (lines 82-91) that builds only the shell and a `newestSourceMtime` (line 106) that ignores tsconfig.build.json. None of that is in this tree. verify-frame.mjs:43 imports the shared `buildDesignEditorIfStale` from './build-if-stale.mjs' and calls it at line 122, immediately before `boot()` starts vite on the consumer fixture — with a comment at lines 113-121 that explicitly documents the exact trap the reviewer says is unfixed. Lines 82-91 are the `shutdown()` helper and line 106 is inside the health-poll loop; the string `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts` does not occur in the file. The shared helper covers BOTH artefacts (build-if-stale.mjs:40 `ARTEFACTS = ['dist/shell/index.html', 'dist/plugin/index.js']`) and DOES include tsconfig.build.json in the staleness input (build-if-stale.mjs:54), building via the package's own `pnpm run build` (line 74). build-if-stale.mjs:6-12 names verify-frame as precisely the consumer that motivated extracting the helper. Additionally the scripts directory contains only build-if-stale.mjs, verify-consumer.mjs and verify-frame.mjs — the `verify-scenes.mjs`/`verify-tokens.mjs` the finding cites do not exist here, indicating the finding was written against a different revision. The "fourth consumer" is updated.
